pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/commands.rs:28 spawns a session with a cwd and no declared write set, so N sessions share one repo with no disjointness check; and src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/stale.rs:640 writes session.state inline instead of through one transition door.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/registry.rs:727 - state is mutated by ~12 sibling methods (set_state_direct, mark_alive, revive_to_running_on_activity, mark_exited, escalate_to_awaiting, park_recovered, mark_finished, finish_unanswered) plus direct writes in stale.rs:640/664/700, each re-implementing its own legality guard; there is no single (state, observation) transition door, so a new observation kind can be mapped inconsistently in one lane, and the entry carries no write-scope claim to release on exit. The closed vocabulary itself IS single-sourced (types.rs:25-97).

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/stale.rs:414 - tick_once performs the staleness check but never asks the OS whether the recorded child_pid is alive and never runs an orphan scan; orphan detection is a frontend 60s poll gated on page mount and window visibility (src/features/plugins/fleet/useFleetOrphanScan.ts:22,38) that only badges a count, so a claude process that outlives the app is unaccounted until a human opens the Fleet page. The rest of tier one/tier two is exemplary: three provenance-separated recency stamps (registry.rs:264-270), a per-workload staleness multiplier with its reason written down (stale.rs:91), and baseline-at-first-sweep revival of spurious awaits (stale.rs:577-600).

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/persist.rs:150 - every restored row becomes a dozing tombstone with child_pid=None regardless of whether its process survived, so reconciliation never reaches 'alive -> adopt' or 'ambiguous -> quarantine'; and src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/run.rs:191 builds the run harvest from FleetSessionRow, making the crash-recovery mirror a user-facing query surface whose writes are best-effort and warn-only (persist.rs:82-86). The piggyback write path (persist.rs:15-19,103) and the identity-not-handles projection (persist.rs:122) are exactly right.

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/registry.rs:1058 - hibernate() kills the child immediately with no quiesce or bounded grace, and the manual path passes require_resting=false (commands.rs:175), so an operator sleeping a Running session loses the in-flight turn and the entry records no interrupt marker for the resume to see. Everything else is conformant and unusually complete: two park depths (doze at registry.rs:1095), policy re-validation inside the lock (registry.rs:1046-1056), restart recovery reusing the doze path (persist.rs:23-26), edge-checked wake (resume_target registry.rs:1328) and lineage adoption (registry.rs:1305).

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/commands.rs:28 - no session declares a write set and no admission check proves disjointness; the DTO comment at types.rs:152-155 actively encourages 'multiple parallel sessions on the same project', so two claude sessions in one repo is a supported configuration with collision detection nowhere. The cap is also enforced by eviction rather than queueing (commands.rs:41 free_slot_for_spawn, stale.rs:1520) and there is no per-member deadline or straggler reaper at mint. The slot cap itself (stale.rs:154) and the run roster (run.rs:59) do exist.

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/run.rs:206 - roster accounting has three buckets and '_ => active_count' swallows stale, lost, awaiting-input and running into one class; a session that reported finished but whose declared summary is unreadable still counts as finished_count (run.rs:207 vs 226), so 'succeeded, result missing' cannot be seen, and there is no straggler deadline, so a run can never be declared closed. The result contract is otherwise exact: summary_from_reason (run.rs:169-183) reports only what a session declared and never a paraphrase, and finish_unanswered (registry.rs:1265) deliberately refuses the completion prefix for a session that only ever asked a question.

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/registry.rs:1234 - mark_finished accepts a FLEET:DONE declaration at face value and parks the session in Finished with the model's own summary; nothing checks the claim against the artifact even though the transcript rollup already knows files_touched (run.rs:228), so a fabricated completion enters the run report as a delivered result. No per-member step budget is set at dispatch either.

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/commands.rs:31 - this module transports the task as an opaque args vector and never authors it; brief composition lives in the dispatcher (companion/approvals/approval_exec_fleet.rs) and in engine/build_session/fanout.rs, so the technique's decision rules have no subject here.

The fleet is task-parallel - N sessions, N tasks, one claude binary; no seat ever answers the same question as another, so the precondition (one question across independently trained members) does not hold.

Sessions are local PTY children of the orchestrator process (registry.rs:290-311 holds master/writer inline); there is no executor plane separated from the control plane, so the dial-out topology question does not arise in these paths.

The substrate is in-process PTY children reaped by their own task; there is no container, volume or worktree daemon holding an inventory that can drift from the registry. The related orphan-process gap is recorded once, under lifecycle-signals.

No post-mortem lane classifies failed multi-session runs. The repo's stale_kind taxonomy (types.rs:210-218) answers a different question - why is this session parked - not which of specification/misalignment/verification owned a run failure.

pairs.registryProposal: durable-fleet-state's 'the mirror is not a query surface' rule is stated absolutely, but this repo has a legitimate second reader: a harvest that must survive an orchestrator restart can only account a roster from the durable copy, because the in-memory registry forgot the sessions that ended before the crash. Worth a paragraph on the one sanctioned second reader (post-hoc run accounting) and the freshness contract it then owes, rather than leaving implementers to violate the rule silently.

pairs.evidence: src/lib/harness/types.ts:3 declares an autonomous Plan -> Execute -> Verify loop over a codebase; its 'scenario' is a set of quality goals with gate commands (scenario-parser.ts:23-56), not an input with an expected property, and nothing here scores a model's output, runs a cell N times, or pins a judge.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/harness/scenario-parser.ts:23 - a ScenarioGoal is a title, a description and prose successCriteria for the repository; it is a specification, not a versioned fixture with an input and a declared expected property, so scenario identity and cache-key scoping have no subject.

pairs.registryProposal: Corrected pairing, and it matters: src/lib/harness is governed by quality-gates, which the matcher never proposed (it paired on the word 'harness'). Judged against quality-gates the context carries a severe deviation on severity-by-construction and gate-liveness: every custom audit gate's command ends in `| wc -l` (verifier.ts:41-53, 57-70), so the pipeline's exit status is wc's and is always 0; runGate returns passed:true whenever execSync does not throw (verifier.ts:104-110), and the '0 means pass' branch that would interpret the count lives in the catch block (verifier.ts:116-125), which those gates can never reach. The result is a gate that reports 37 violations as a pass. Both audits are also `required:false` while verify() counts only required failures (verifier.ts:143-150), so the severity label is neutralized twice over. Recommend adding the quality-gates pair to this context in the map.

pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/engine/src/eval.rs:607 pins the judge to DEFAULT_BALANCED, which is an alias for SONNET_CURRENT (src-tauri/core/src/model_ids.rs:44), so the pin moves whenever the alias is bumped and no run records which judge produced it; and eval.rs:380 folds three metrics into one weighted composite scored from a single run.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/engine/src/eval.rs:605-607 - the intent is right and documented ('Pinned deliberately so scoring runs on a consistent judge rather than the undeclared account default'), but the pin resolves through DEFAULT_BALANCED -> SONNET_CURRENT (src-tauri/core/src/model_ids.rs:44): bumping the alias silently re-judges every future run against a different instrument, and the run artifact records the model only in the spend ledger (eval.rs:654), not against the score. src-tauri/engine/src/eval.rs:380 - tool_accuracy, output_quality and protocol_compliance are combined by fixed weights into one composite with `passed: Some(composite_score >= 50)` (eval.rs:400), so a high score on one dimension buys a failing score on another and no dimension is declared the constraint. One half IS right, and is the important half: confusion detection is a hard threshold that overrides the composite to zero rather than being weighted into it (eval.rs:366-379).

src-tauri/engine/src/eval.rs:400 - a verdict is rendered from a single run with no N, no declared aggregation and no variance; the `confidence` field beside it (eval.rs:116,129,161) is a hardcoded per-branch heuristic, not a measurement over repeated trials, so a score that travels carries no aggregation rule and flakiness is invisible rather than reported.

pairs.registryProposal: Two notes. (1) The brief's path src-tauri/engine/src/test_runner.rs no longer exists - the map row is stale for this context. pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: Five independent sites default an unrecognized severity to the mildest bucket (ReviewListItem.tsx:11, ReviewDetailPanel.tsx:116, reviewFocusHelpers.tsx:107 and :143, ReviewFocusFlow.tsx:46) with no marker, and this repo auto-resolves reviews unattended overnight - the exact composition fail-loud-classification-default warns about.

techniques.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_manual-review/components/ReviewListItem.tsx:11 - `SEVERITY_LABELS[severity] ?? 'Info'`, repeated at ReviewDetailPanel.tsx:116, reviewFocusHelpers.tsx:107, reviewFocusHelpers.tsx:143 and ReviewFocusFlow.tsx:46, and again in the shared severityBucket (src/features/fleet/monitor/monitorModel.ts:49-53). An item whose severity payload cannot be read takes the quietest bucket, carries no marker saying why, and - because Night Shift resolves approvals unattended (documented at src/lib/decisions/rowWrites.ts:22-25) - a genuinely critical event with an unreadable payload can be waved through with nobody having seen it.

src/features/overview/sub_manual-review/libs/reviewHelpers.ts:60-87 - whether a verdict was made by a human or by machine policy is recovered by regex over free-text reviewer_notes, with the comment stating outright 'there is no structured auto_resolved column'. The decider is therefore not a field: a reworded backend note silently reclassifies an auto-approval as a human decision, and the record cannot answer who decided.

src/features/overview/sub_manual-review/hooks/useManualReviewQueue.ts:7 - the queue's status vocabulary is pending/approved/rejected/resolved with no deadline, overdue state or terminal action anywhere, and the filter bar offers status, source and persona but never age (ReviewFilterTrailing.tsx:19-28); a pending decision is immortal, so nothing gets louder as it waits and no severity has a declared clock.

src/lib/decisions/rowWrites.ts:1-30 - one write door per decidable row type, every door rejects on a failed write, and every door carries the status the caller saw so the backend turns it into a compare-and-swap; a verdict written against a row somebody else already decided loses loudly (isDecisionConflict) rather than overwriting, which is transition authority separated from work authority done in code.

src/features/overview/sub_manual-review/components/BulkActionBar.tsx:30 - homogeneous items are one decision with an explicit confirm step, and the queue stays O(viewport) at any volume through server-side status/persona filters, keyset paging and a counts layer that badges without loading rows (useManualReviewQueue.ts:22-33).

The surface does render an auto-resolution badge with the machine's reasoning (AutoResolvedBadge.tsx via reviewHelpers.ts:78-85), but whether the grant is scoped, expiring and audited is decided in engine/dispatch.rs and engine/auto_triage.rs, outside these paths.

Approving a review that carries assignment_id/step_id resumes a held team step, but the continuation runs backend-side; I did not verify that approve resumes without re-generation or that reject leaves no zombie.
This is the review flow - the machine has already produced something and a human rules on it. The consent flow (first use, impact disclosure, autonomy dial) lives in the vault autoCred context.
No step here is one the machine must not perform; the human decides and the machine acts.

The invariant holds between two ladders - an urgency ladder that only paints and an enforcing ladder that acts. This queue has neither: no elapsed-time styling and no timed terminal action, so there is no pair to order.
The queue rules on completed items; it never carries an executor's scope record or a route it may amend mid-run.

pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: The whole gate lives in component state: AutoCredPanel.tsx:70-83 kills the browser session on unmount and handleCancel resets it, so a guided runbook the operator navigates away from loses its position, the values already supplied, and any record that consent was ever given. One root cause, three unmet obligations.

techniques.evidence: src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/autoCred/steps/AutoCredConsent.tsx:60 - informed consent with a numbered what-will-happen disclosure specific to the chosen mode, a security notice, the connector's own docs, and explicit start/cancel, all before any browser touches the user's account; and the human then decides on the real thing, not a summary - AutoCredReview.tsx:5 renders the actual extracted values in editable capture rows with a partial-extraction warning and a healthcheck before save. Consent is re-asked every time rather than remembered, which is the safe direction of the first-use rule.

src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/autoCred/steps/AutoCredPanel.tsx:70 - the guided mode IS the runbook the technique asks for (a sequenced five-step flow that holds state, prompts for exactly what only the person can supply, and verifies via healthcheck: AutoCredConsent.tsx:63-70), but it does not resume where it stopped - unmount cancels the browser session and handleCancel calls session.reset() - and it hands back no record of what ran and what was verified: the run log is ephemeral component state rendered by AutoCredLogEntries.tsx, copyable at best.

src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/autoCred/steps/AutoCredPanel.tsx:53 - the gate's state is `session.phase` inside a React hook, so the pending question exists only in a running component's memory; a remount re-opens the gate at 'consent' (the file documents a prior bug where a re-render bounced the phase back, lines 91-97) and a crash or navigation discards it silently rather than leaving durable pending state.

src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/autoCred/steps/AutoCredPanel.tsx:117 - onConsent is `session.startBrowser`, a local phase advance; authorizing a browser to drive the user's live account and extract credential material leaves no durable who/what/when/on-which-version/having-seen-what, so the authorization cannot be audited or bounded afterwards.

src/features/vault/sub_catalog/components/autoCred/steps/AutoCredPanel.tsx:77-83 - the reject/abandon path is explicit cleanup, not a zombie: the effect cancels a live browser session through a ref that always targets the current session rather than a stale closure, and handleCancel resets before handing control back.
The flow is synchronous and single-item with the operator present; there is no queue of pending judgments to batch or triage.
The flow cannot run unattended by construction - the guided mode exists precisely because a person must perform the login step.
Nothing here is classified by severity or waits on a deadline; the human is at the keyboard for the duration.
Neither an urgency ladder nor an enforcing one exists in this flow.
No payload is classified into severity buckets here; a failed extraction is surfaced as a typed error display (AutoCredErrorDisplay) rather than bucketed.
There is no executor operating under a scope record; the machine follows one fixed adapter sequence chosen at start (playwright or guided).

pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/build_session/tool_tests.rs:1-6 has a scratch Claude CLI compose the test plan, and oneshot.rs:215 re-runs it after every fix pass, so the oracle is re-authored by a model inside the repair loop it is meant to judge.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/build_session/tool_tests.rs:1-6 - the test plan is composed fresh by a spawned CLI on each attempt, and oneshot.rs:215 loops fix -> re-test up to MAX_TEST_RETRIES, so 'make it pass' has a second solution the green result cannot distinguish: a weaker plan. There is no red-first ordering (the check is authored in the same cycle as the fix). Two code-authored fences bound how weak it can get - the platform-builtin allow-list is CODE a model cannot extend (tool_tests.rs:66-80) and an unexecuted entry classifies as unverified rather than pass - but the oracle itself is not read-only to the fixer.

src-tauri/src/engine/build_session/tool_tests.rs:1-6 - the blocking verdict is produced by live curl calls against third-party APIs, so the same draft can be refused tomorrow by an upstream outage nobody here caused; worse, a transient 5xx lands as tools_failed, which routes to Failed rather than Held (oneshot.rs:373-379) and spends the fix-pass budget rewriting a correct agent_ir. The invocation is not split into a deterministic half that blocks and an externally-fed half that reports.

src-tauri/src/engine/build_session/oneshot.rs:389-396 - the promote predicate used to be `report.get("tools_failed").unwrap_or(0) == 0`, which the file documents as failing OPEN on every malformed shape; it now fails CLOSED, and the exit path from finding to effect is traced in the doc comment rather than asserted by a label.

src-tauri/src/engine/build_session/tool_tests.rs:52-58 - `unverified` is a third outcome distinct from pass and fail ('an LLM boolean is not a call', 'a vault row is not a test'), and it HOLDS promotion (oneshot.rs:366-379) without being reported as a failure; a hole in the gate's instrument therefore never reads as compliance.

src-tauri/src/engine/build_session/oneshot.rs:398-407 - the instrument is asserted before the result (shape, then integrity, then verdict), including a cross-check that the declared counts do not undercount what the results array actually contains, and roughly twenty unit tests around the predicate (oneshot.rs:981-1334) feed it known-bad reports and assert it holds.

src-tauri/src/engine/build_session/oneshot.rs:362-368 - one Held reason string is the single enumeration every surface renders: error_message, the OS notification body and the companion-chat episode, with the full detail kept in last_test_report, so no projection can understate what blocked.

src-tauri/src/engine/build_session/tool_tests.rs:56-58 - the unverified class exists so the fix-pass model does not 'burn retries trying to correct' something that never failed; the trust budget being protected belongs to an automated repairer rather than a human, and the reasoning is identical.

The cost tiers are right in shape - cheap capability gates during the conversation (gates.rs:13-20), the expensive real-API run at promote - but I did not verify the binding-rung invariant, that every gated field checked during the conversation is re-validated at promote.
No committed baseline exists for any metric here; the gate is a hard pass/hold, with nothing that may only fall.
There is no version-control hook in this context; the gate runs inside a build session, not in an author's working tree.
No routing convention is being proven here - there is no wrapper whose call sites need a bijection against a registry.

pairs.registryProposal: blocking-by-input-determinism reads as if the gated subject is always a code tree, and prescribes 'split the invocation so the deterministic half blocks'. This context is the case the rule does not cover: the gated act is ARMING a live integration against real credentials and a public webhook, so a verdict that never touched the third party is exactly the false green the gate exists to prevent (tool_tests.rs:37-42 settles this explicitly). The repo's answer is better than the technique's - keep the externally-fed gate blocking, but give it a third terminal outcome (Held: refuse to promote, spend no repair budget) distinct from Failed. Recommend the technique name that outcome for externally-fed gates whose subject is an irreversible activation, and pair it with the corollary this repo has NOT applied: an upstream transport failure must classify as Held, not Failed.

pairs.subject: self-healing
pairs.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_incidents/libs/incidentTaxonomy.ts:64 ranks an unrecognized severity at 0 - below `low` - and groupIncidents.ts:33 uses that rank to pick a group's worst severity, so unclassifiable incidents sort quieter than everything else instead of louder.

techniques.evidence: src/features/overview/sub_incidents/libs/groupIncidents.ts:5 - the inbox groups by agent, severity, source or nothing; there is no signature dimension, so recurring failures are never deduped into one louder row carrying their healing history, and nothing counts recurrence. Compounding it, incidentTaxonomy.ts:64 returns rank 0 for an unknown severity while severityBadgeClass paints it `medium` (line 57), so worstSeverityOf (groupIncidents.ts:33-38) can rank a group of unclassified incidents below a group of `low` - the failures the healer could not classify get quieter over time, the inverse of what the technique requires.

src/features/overview/sub_incidents/components/IncidentsInboxKpiHeader.tsx:28-36 - the only outcome vocabulary on this surface is the human-triage triple open/acknowledged/resolved; there is no confirmed-fixed vs reverted vs unknown split and no per-strategy-per-category rate, so a heal that was rolled back and a heal that worked both land as `resolved` and an operator cannot answer 'did it help' from the surface the subject says must answer it.

src/features/overview/sub_incidents/libs/incidentTaxonomy.ts:13-22 - the surface consumes the source and severity the backend row already carries across nine authorities and never re-derives a category from message text; an unrecognized source echoes its raw token (line 52) rather than being folded into an invented class, and IncidentDetailBreakdown.tsx:35 renders an empty detail as an explicit 'no detail' instead of a blank.
The precedence tree and its mutual exclusions live in the healing engine; this read-only inbox selects no strategy and can express no 'do nothing, recorded with its reason'.
The allowlist of what a healer may mutate, and the consent gates on its risky tiers, are enforced backend-side; nothing in this context authorizes or bounds a mutation.
Watching aggregate error rates in a healing change's wake and undoing it is machinery designed at apply time; this surface neither observes the attribution window nor triggers a revert.

pairs.subject: import-normalization
pairs.evidence: There is no loss ledger: N8nParserResults.tsx:57-59 counts only the tools, triggers and connectors that survived, never reconciling them against the element count the detector found, and the IR (src/lib/types/designTypes.ts:70-94) carries neither a conversion grade nor provenance.

techniques.evidence: src/features/templates/sub_n8n/steps/N8nParserResults.tsx:57 - toolCount / triggerCount / connectorCount are counts of what was produced, shown without their predicate; nothing enumerates the foreign node types that did not map, no entity carries a conversion grade (mapped cleanly / approximated / inert / dropped), and the only 'unmapped' surface in the whole context is a connector warning in the wizard footer (N8nWizardFooter.tsx:94). The detector already knows the source element count (workflowDetector.ts:22), so 'imported 40 of 50' is computable and is not computed - the four hours of rebuilding stay hidden until runtime.

src/lib/types/designTypes.ts:70-94 - AgentIR is a genuine narrow waist that all four platform adapters lower into, but it carries no provenance (source format, source version, foreign identifier) and no loss ledger; `platform` travels beside it as a view prop (N8nParserResults.tsx:22), so a committed persona keeps no record of which foreign format and version produced it and re-import collision detection has nothing to key on.

src/lib/personas/parsers/workflowDetector.ts:10-24 - DetectionResult carries platform, confidence and format but no version stamp, and the walk always returns exactly one platform, so the technique's ambiguity outcome (more than one candidate, resolved with the user) cannot be expressed and the operator-posture counter 'detection outcomes by format and version' cannot exist. The rest is strong: structural fingerprints not extensions, ordered discriminators, an honest `unknown` platform, format-constrained candidates (FORMAT_PLATFORMS, line 39), and one walk in which the count always comes from the collection that named the platform - the file documents the two-table divergence bug that rule was written to kill (lines 50-63).

src/features/templates/sub_n8n/steps/N8nParserResultsSections.tsx:24 - per-entity opt-in via SelectionCheckbox on every tool, trigger and connector rather than all-or-nothing, ahead of the commit step; and N8nParserResults.tsx:23-26 carries `platformNeedsConfirmation` - 'True when platform was guessed and needs user confirmation' - which is exactly the one bit of state that separates disciplined speculative adaptation from a silent fall-through into the most permissive parser.

src/features/templates/sub_n8n/steps/upload/n8nUploadTypes.ts:2-8 - the size cap is imported from a GENERATED mirror of the Rust authority (n8nLimits.generated, 'Single source of truth: src-tauri/src/commands/design/n8n_limits.rs') and bounds file, paste and URL modes alike before deserialization; discovered credential material is routed out as `connectorsNeedingSetup` requirements the user fulfils rather than persisted with the entities (confirm/n8nConfirmTypes.ts:10), and per-entity failures come back itemized as EntityError rather than as a partial silent commit. Depth caps were not verified.

The detector's own tables are declarative data (workflowDetector.ts:27-41), but the node-type and parameter maps that do the actual adapting live in the Rust parser, outside the listed paths; the standard already asserts a dated finding about this repo ('left its mapping tables as two hand-maintained twins') which I did not re-verify and will not restate as a verdict.
